May WASDE report to reveal first look at new crop outlook

What will the USDA have to say about the 2026 crop, and how will that impact prices?

May 11, 2026

The USDA's May World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates report, releasing tomorrow at 12:00 p.m. Eastern, will provide the first official glimpse into the 2026-27 marketing year projections for corn, soybeans, and wheat.

Corn projections hold steady

Old crop corn ending stocks are expected to remain unchanged from April at approximately 2.1 billion bushels, according to Reuters trader surveys. New crop estimates average 1.9 billion bushels, based on 95.3 million planted acres and a trend-line yield of 183 bushels per acre. Export demand continues performing above expectations, potentially triggering small upward revisions.

Soybeans face mixed demand signals

Soybean old crop ending stocks should hold near 345.5 million bushels, but the demand picture shows contrasts. Domestic crush jumped 10% year-over-year in March, while export shipments lag the five-year pace. Brazilian competition intensified with an 18% surge in soybean export values, contributing to that country's record $10.5 billion April trade surplus.

Related:New phosphate plant promises domestic fertilizer boost by 2028

Wheat exports exceed targets

Wheat export sales have already reached 100% of USDA's target, well ahead of the five-year average. Analysts anticipate modest upward demand revisions, with old crop ending stocks forecast near 934 million bushels and new crop around 820 million.

The report's projections remain subject to actual planting progress and growing season conditions.
